findings.title: Bind scientific helper compatibility at both case admission points
findings.body: If a scientific change is made only in full_noise_probe_inputs.py, original_noise_source.py, cached_mode_source0.py, or an imported physical/projection helper, this binding_contract remains unchanged. reusable() consequently accepts earlier successful generations, and load_case() never checks the recorded implementation lists or a scientific operator/projection compatibility identity; the same unchecked loader also admits explicit --done inputs during final aggregation. A resumed batch can therefore mix sectors evaluated with incompatible force or covariance definitions while reporting complete coverage. Carry and validate a scientific compatibility identity through the producer, reuse, and aggregation boundaries, covering those helpers; preserve explicitly established compatibility for metadata-only edits rather than blindly invalidating old valid data for every recorded file-byte change.

The producer checks it before work and emits scientific_compatibility_identity. load_context checks the profile and original plan; load_case explicitly calls admit_result for both direct --done aggregation and batch reuse. New results require the matching identity; pre-identity results require an exact original-record/result path/bytes/SHA entry in the four-result retrospective allowlist. Batch reuse retains immutable original-input/plan/paid-packet joins and successful durable exit/stream authentication while treating incidental implementation byte metadata as provenance, avoiding recomputation solely for the explicitly classified admission/publication-only edits.

findings.title: Persist checkpoint directory entries before accepting completion
findings.body: The producer fsyncs result.json and done.json file contents but never fsyncs their containing case directory. The runner's later outcome/accepted writes fsync the generation directory, not case/, so they do not establish durability of those two checkpoint names. A host crash can therefore lose a supposedly committed completion and cause a completed physical sector to be recomputed. Fresh generation/run directories likewise are created without syncing the directories containing their new names. Fsync the directories whose entries are published, including the case result/done entries and newly created checkpoint-directory ancestors, before declaring the work durable.
findings.location_basis: Original reviewed patch location, retained for historical finding identity.
findings.resolution: Producer save_json now synchronizes the containing case directory after fsyncing each exclusive file. Producer case and batch root/run/generation creation use make_directory, whose recursive missing-parent creation synchronizes each directory and the parent owning its name. Both result and completion publication use the corrected helper without changing result-before-done ordering or non-overwrite semantics.
resolution_evidence: checkpoint_directories.py:6-12 fsyncs a directory descriptor with finally-close; lines15-30 recursively create missing parents and synchronize each directory plus containing parent.

batch_mode_noise.py:74 creates generations durably; lines211-213 durably create batch/run directories. Existing aggregate save_json still fsyncs both file and parent directory.

findings.title: Stop and drain active cases before executor shutdown
findings.body: When a parent-side exception escapes the scheduling/readout loop while another case is active, for example an OSError from the fsynced progress write or a rejection receipt write, the ThreadPoolExecutor context exits before this outer handler sets stop. Its __exit__ waits for workers, so live physical producers continue until their own timeout, batch deadline, or normal completion instead of being stopped on the parent failure. The loop is then abandoned without consuming the remaining futures, so even successfully written child outcomes are absent from the run's completed/cost accounting. Set stop and drain/reconcile active futures inside the executor scope on exceptional exits, before its blocking shutdown.
findings.location_basis: Original reviewed patch location, retained for historical finding identity.
findings.resolution: An inner executor exception handler now sets stop before blocking shutdown and consumes all remaining active futures. One drained publication failure is retained in drain_errors without preventing other drains. consume first waits for its worker and reloads the durable outcome, then appends outcome/failure/completion accounting before fallible publication. Missing outcomes or measurements remain explicit rather than disappearing or becoming zero; an admitted completed case stays completed even if accepted/progress publication subsequently fails.
resolution_evidence: batch_mode_noise.py:258-329 reconciles each owned future; failure accounting precedes rejection writes and completed accounting precedes accepted/progress writes.
batch_mode_noise.py:282-297 explicitly accounts missing outcomes/measurements; lines225-243 propagate unknown costs as null and count measured/unmeasured separately.
batch_mode_noise.py:378-423 keeps stop-and-drain inside the ThreadPoolExecutor scope; lines410-422 drain other workers despite individual errors.
Final summary includes drain_errors and per-outcome measurement evidence instead of silently omitting unsettled work.
